title: Random coordinate selection never loses to magnitude selection at matched delivery on SmolLM2-135M; the two primary contrasts are undecided because one threshold seed in each diverged, and a 50% random writer at lr 1e-4 ties tuned fp32 master
headline: Delivering a uniformly random fraction of each AdamW update (keno) gives lower held-out NLL than delivering the same cumulative amount through the coordinates with the largest relative update (threshold) in all six matched cells; the mean keno minus threshold difference over the six cells is -0.0187 nats and magnitude wins none. The two pre-registered primary contrasts are undecided under the interval rule (25% @ 2e-4: -0.0273 [-0.0593, +0.0048]; 50% @ 1e-4: -0.0122 [-0.0292, +0.0048]) because one threshold seed in each cell diverged late in training (NLL 1.2405 and 1.1976); the four secondary contrasts all have 90% intervals entirely below zero (random wins). The tuned keno writer, 50% @ lr 1e-4, ties tuned fp32 master @ 5e-5: +0.0009 [-0.0003, +0.0020], and three other keno configurations are within 0.003 of the same bar. Plain bf16 rounding sits above the keno delivery-loss curve at both learning rates (-0.0169 at 2e-4, interpolated; -0.0347 at 1e-4, a short extrapolation below the 15% level).
research_question: Given that a random 25% keno write distributor reproduced plain bf16 rounding's advantage over fp32 master, does it matter which coordinates receive the update? Compare random selection (keno-drop) with magnitude-based selection (threshold-drop: |update|/bf16 spacing >= theta) at matched cumulative delivery and identical exact-write precision; test whether a tuned keno writer beats tuned exact delivery; and locate plain rounding on the keno delivery-loss curve.

decision_rules.q1: paired per seed over five seeds, 90% Student-t interval of NLL(keno_drop_f) - NLL(thr_drop_f matched to it): entirely < 0 random wins; entirely > 0 magnitude wins; inside +-0.01 indistinguishable; otherwise undecided. Primary: 25% @ 2e-4 and 50% @ 1e-4; 15% level and the remaining cells secondary.
decision_rules.q2: paired per seed, 90% interval of NLL(keno_drop_50 @ 1e-4) - NLL(fp32_master @ 5e-5 from exp_01m1tgnb6xf98sqwfhm4effknt): entirely < 0 beats; inside +-0.01 tie; otherwise as reported. Other configurations exploratory.
decision_rules.q3: descriptive: per lr and seed, keno_drop NLL linearly interpolated over the keno curve at rne's measured delivery, minus rne's NLL
decision_rules.divergent_runs: researcher instruction: report thr_drop_25@2e-4 seed 2 and thr_drop_50@1e-4 seed 1 as-is, do not exclude, characterise with clip counts and per-step selected fractions

methods.model: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M @ 93efa2f097d58c2a74874c7e644dbc9b0cee75a2, bfloat16 parameters and moments, CompensatedAdamW with a write distributor
methods.data: gsm8k main @ 740312add88f781978c0658806c59bc2815b9866; 3000 steps, batch size 1, seed-specific fixed order; held-out NLL on 49,277 tokens
methods.selectors: keno-drop f: every 50 steps redraw a uniform random mask covering fraction f of coordinates; drawn coordinates get the exact write t = p + i + c, p <- rne(t), c <- t - p; undrawn requests are discarded. threshold-drop theta: every step select coordinates with |i| / spacing(p) >= theta (spacing = 2^(exponent-7)); same exact write on selected coordinates, unselected discarded.
methods.calibration: theta per (lr, level) chosen on seed 0 by a secant search on the full 3000-step run until the threshold writer's cumulative delivery (sum of realised update length / sum of intended update length) matched keno's within 0.02; the converged pass is the seed-0 production record. theta = {"thr_drop_15@0.0001": 0.35, "thr_drop_15@0.0002": 0.5868, "thr_drop_25@0.0001": 0.2, "thr_drop_25@0.0002": 0.3088, "thr_drop_50@0.0001": 0.06, "thr_drop_50@0.0002": 0.1022}
methods.grid: levels 15%, 25%, 50% x lr 2e-4, 1e-4 x seeds 0-4 for both selectors (keno 25%/50% seeds 0,1 from exp_01m1tvjx4ee3xshh9djt6db5bx); reference rne, fp32_master, kahan, torch_adamw from exp_01m1tgnb6xf98sqwfhm4effknt
methods.harness_check: rne seed 2 lr 2e-4 rerun in this pipeline reproduced 1.163403438942883 with |diff| 0.0 and all 3000 per-step losses identical
methods.compute: one H100 per job, three concurrent jobs; keno about 0.13 s/step, threshold about 0.16 s/step
methods.uncertainty: 90% Student-t intervals on paired per-seed differences, n = 5
methods.seeds: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (data order, init and keno mask share the seed)
methods.logging: W&B project default-exp-exp_01m1v355jafe8sqbzmwmmxc06t; 14 threshold runs from Sept 8 trained without W&B after the API handshake failed, their records carry wandb_url null

limitations: Q1 primary verdicts are undecided under the pre-registered interval rule because one threshold seed in each primary cell diverged late in training; the four stable seeds in each cell favour random selection by 0.011 to 0.014 (25% @ 2e-4) and 0.003 to 0.006 (50% @ 1e-4), and excluding the divergent seeds is post-hoc and not done.

Matched cumulative delivery is not matched selection count or schedule: threshold selects 3 to 21% of coordinates per step with an early-heavy decaying schedule while keno selects a flat 15 to 50%, and threshold leaves 20 to 72% of coordinates never moved (norm parameters 63 to 97%) versus 5 to 18% for keno. The Q1 result is therefore about the selection rule as a whole, not about random versus magnitude at equal counts.

The calibrated thetas for the 25% and 50% levels are below the bf16 format's own effective threshold of one half spacing (only 15% @ 2e-4 at theta 0.587 is stricter), so threshold-drop is a softer version of the format's pick rather than a replica; the rounding-overshoot account of plain rounding's position above the keno curve is an interpretation.
Q3 at lr 1e-4 is a short linear extrapolation below the 15% level (rne delivery 0.184 vs keno 15% at 0.195) and is descriptive only.
Single model (SmolLM2-135M), single dataset (GSM8K), batch size 1, 3000 steps.
